parameters.content:
## 1 · The checklist is data, not code

Three tables: the hires, the checklist template, and the tasks actually outstanding.

The checklist is the point. Rows say what applies to everyone, what applies to a role, a department, or an employment type. HR adds one row to give every future mechanic a new induction step and nobody opens this workflow. A checklist buried in a Code node is a checklist that goes stale.

## 2 · Work out what each person needs, then create only what is missing

Six hires and twelve checklist rows become the exact task list each person needs. A cancelled offer is skipped, and the reason is recorded rather than hidden in a query.

Only rows that do not exist yet are written, keyed on hire plus task code. A task somebody already completed is never reset to open by a later run, and running twice in one morning cannot create a duplicate.

## 3 · Ready, on track, at risk, blocked

Ready means every MANDATORY item is done — not every item. Blocked beats everything else, because a blocked task is not a chasing problem and no number of reminders will move it. Those two get very different messages on purpose: dashboards show late and blocked the same colour, and they need opposite responses.

Someone three weeks out with an untouched checklist is deliberately silent. Mailing about them teaches everyone to ignore the mail.

## 4 · Grouped twice, on two different axes

Hires are grouped for the MANAGER — one message about their person. Tasks are grouped for the TEAM that owes them — IT gets a single mail listing everything IT owes across every new starter.

That is the difference between a system people read and one they filter. A team already chased in the last two days is skipped — unless something is overdue, or a day-one item belongs to somebody starting imminently, in which case urgency overrides the gap and the team is chased again.

## 5 · Where it goes

All three are switched off and carry no credential, so the demo runs with nothing to set up. Two things do read the send step: the chase stamp records whether a message genuinely went out, and the report counts real sends rather than intentions — so with the nodes off, both honestly say drafted rather than sent.

Ready and on-track never ping anyone. Only at-risk and blocked reach Slack.

nodes.name: Only Teams Worth Chasing
nodes.notes: The suppression is decided in the engine and enforced here. Without this node the flag is a comment: every team gets mailed every morning and the report quietly claims otherwise.
